segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הָאוֹמֵר: ״כִּתְבוּ גֵּט וּתְנוּ לְאִשְׁתִּי״; ״גָּרְשׁוּהָ״; ״כִּתְבוּ אִיגֶּרֶת וּתְנוּ לַהּ״ – הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ יִכְתְּבוּ וְיִתְּנוּ.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» With regard to a husband «who says» to two people: «Write a bill of divorce and give» it «to my wife,» or: «Divorce her,» or: «Write a letter and give» it «to her, they should write» the document «and give» it to her. In each of those cases his intent is clear. He is instructing them to effect her divorce.

segments.he: ״פַּטְּרוּהָ״; ״פַּרְנְסוּהָ״; ״עֲשׂוּ לָהּ כְּנִימוּס״; ״עֲשׂוּ לָהּ כָּרָאוּי״ – לֹא אָמַר כְּלוּם.
segments.en: However, one who said: «Release her,» or: «Sustain her, or: Treat her according to the law [nimus],» or: «Treat her appropriately, said nothing,» as none of these expressions clearly expresses his desire to divorce his wife.

positions.claim: 'write a get and give', 'divorce her', 'write a letter' are effective; 'release/sustain/treat according to law/appropriately' are nothing
